butir.teks: Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "Whoever seeks knowledge of the kind by which the face of Allah Most High is sought, in order to gain by it some share of this world, will not find the scent of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection." (١) Allah has described the evil scholars as eating this world by means of knowledge, and the scholars of the Hereafter as having humility in prayer (khushu') and renunciation (zuhd). So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said about the scholars of this world, ⟦QS 3:187⟧ and Allah Most High said about the scholars of the Hereafter, ⟦QS 3:199⟧ Some of the early generations (salaf) said, "The scholars are gathered in the company of the prophets, and the judges are gathered in the company of the sultans."
And included in the meaning of the judges is every jurist whose aim is to seek this world by means of his knowledge.
And it was reported

Abu al-Darda' (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), that he said, "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to one of the prophets: Say to those who study jurisprudence for other than the sake of religion, who learn for other than the sake of action, and who seek this world through the work of the Hereafter, who put on for people the skins of rams while their hearts are like the hearts of wolves, their tongues sweeter than honey and their hearts more bitter than aloes: Me they deceive, and at Me they mock! I will surely open for them a trial that leaves the forbearing man bewildered." (١) Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) who said that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "The scholars of this community are two men. One is a man to whom Allah gave knowledge and who gave it freely to people, taking nothing in return out of greed and not buying a price with it. For such a one the birds of the sky, the fish of the water, the beasts of the earth and the noble recording angels pray. He will come before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection as a noble master, until he joins the messengers. The other is a man to whom Allah gave knowledge in this world, and he was stingy with it towards the servants of Allah, took something in return out of greed, and bought a price with it. Such a one will come on the Day of Resurrection bridled with a bridle of fire, and a caller will call out above the heads of creation, 'This is so-and-so, son of so-and-so, to whom Allah gave knowledge in this world, and he was stingy with it towards His servants, took something in return for it out of greed, and bought a price with it.' So he will be punished until the reckoning of the people is finished." (٢) More severe than this is what is reported, that a man used to serve Moses (peace be upon him) and began to say, "Moses, the chosen one of Allah, told me; Moses, the confidant of Allah, told me; Moses, the one Allah spoke to, told me," until he became rich and his wealth grew large. Moses (peace be upon him) missed him and began to ask about him, but could find no news of him, until one day a man came to him with a pig in his hand and a black rope around its neck. Moses (peace be upon him) said to him, "Do you know so-and-so?" The man said, "Yes." Then he said, "He is this pig." Moses said, "My Lord, I ask You to restore him to his former state so that I may ask him by what this befell him." So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him, "If you called upon Me with that by which Adam called upon Me, or anyone below him, I would not answer you concerning him. But I will tell you why I did this to him: because he used to seek this world through religion." Graver still is what Mu'adh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him) reported, as his own words and, in one narration, as traced to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), saying, "Part of the trial of the scholar is that speaking is dearer to him than listening." (٣) In speech there is embellishment and excess, and its speaker is not safe from error, while in silence there is safety and knowledge. Among the scholars are some who store up their knowledge and do not like it to be found with anyone else; such a one is in the first level of the Fire. And among the scholars are some who, in regard to their knowledge, are in the position of a sultan: if anything of his knowledge is rejected, or any of his right is made light of, he becomes angry; such a one is in the second level of the Fire.

And among the scholars are some who keep their knowledge and the rare hadiths they know for people of honour and wealth, and do not regard the needy as deserving of it; such a one is in the third level of the Fire.
And among the scholars are some who set themselves up to give legal rulings and so give rulings in error, and Allah Most High hates those who overreach; such a one is in the fourth level of the Fire.
And among the scholars are some who speak the words of the Jews and the Christians so that their knowledge may seem abundant; such a one is in the fifth level of the Fire.
And among the scholars are some who take their knowledge as a means to manliness (muru'a), distinction and renown among people; such a one is in the sixth level of the Fire.

And among the scholars are some who are stirred up by vanity and self-admiration ('ujb): if he admonishes, he is harsh, and if he is admonished, he is disdainful; such a one is in the seventh level of the Fire.
So hold to silence, my brother; by it you overcome Satan. And beware of laughing without something to wonder at, or walking without need.

In another report: "A servant may have praise spread for him that fills what is between the east and the west, while he does not weigh with Allah the wing of a gnat." (٤) It is reported that a man from Khurasan carried to al-Hasan, after his leaving his gathering, a purse containing five thousand dirhams and ten garments of fine cloth (bazz), and said, "Abu Sa'id, this is for expenses and this is clothing." Al-Hasan said, "May Allah Most High grant you well-being. Keep your expenses and your clothing, for we have no need of that. Indeed, whoever
sits in a gathering like this one of mine and accepts from people the like of this will meet Allah Most High on the Day of Resurrection having no share."

It is reported from Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him), both as his own words and as traced to the Prophet, that he said that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "Do not sit with every scholar, except a scholar who calls you from five to five: from doubt to certainty, from showing off (riya') to sincerity, from craving to renunciation, from arrogance to humility, and from enmity to sincere advice." (١) Allah Most High said, ⟦QS 28:79-80⟧ the verse. So the people of knowledge are known by their preferring the Hereafter over this world.

Among them is that his deed does not contradict his word; rather, he does not command anything unless he is the first to act upon it. Allah Most High said, ⟦QS 2:44⟧ and Allah Most High said, ⟦QS 61:3⟧ and Allah Most High said in the story of Shu'ayb, ⟦QS 11:88⟧ and Allah Most High said, ⟦QS 2:282⟧ and Allah Most High said. And Allah Most High said to Jesus (peace be upon him), "Son of Mary, admonish yourself; if you take the admonition, then admonish people, and if not, be ashamed before Me." And the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "On the night I was taken on the night journey I passed by people whose lips were being cut with scissors of fire. I said, 'Who are you?' They said, 'We used to command what is good and not do it, and to forbid evil and do it.'" (٢) And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "The ruin of my community is a wicked scholar and an ignorant worshipper. The worst of the worst are the worst of the scholars, and the best of the best are the best of the scholars." (٣) Al-Awza'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "The tombs complained of what they suffered from the stench of the corpses of the unbelievers, so Allah revealed to them, 'The bellies of the evil scholars are more foul-smelling than what you are in.'"
Al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "It has reached me that the sinful among the scholars will be begun with on the Day of Resurrection, before the idol worshippers."
Abu al-Darda' (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "Woe to the one who does not know, once; and woe to the one who knows and does not act, seven times."

Al-Sha'bi said, "On the Day of Resurrection some people of Paradise will look down upon some people of the Fire and say to them, 'What brought you into the Fire, when Allah only admitted us to Paradise through the favour of your instructing and teaching us?' They will reply, 'We used to command what is good and not do it, and to forbid evil and do it.'"

Hatim al-Asamm (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "On the Day of Resurrection there is no one more regretful than a man who taught people knowledge, and they acted upon it while he did not act upon it, so they succeeded because of him and he perished."
Malik ibn Dinar said, "When the scholar does not act upon his knowledge, his admonition slips off the hearts as raindrops slip off a smooth rock." And they recited:

O preacher to the people, you have become suspect,
for you find fault in them with things that you yourself commit.

You have begun advising them with preaching, striving hard,
yet the ruinous sins, by my life, are what you yourself commit.

You find fault with this world and with people who desire it,
while you desire it more than they do.
And another said:

Do not forbid a trait while doing the like of it;
it is a great disgrace for you if you do so.

Ibrahim ibn Adham (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "I passed by a stone in Mecca on which was written, 'Turn me over and you will take a lesson.' So I turned it over, and on it was written, 'You do not act on what you know, so how do you seek knowledge of what you do not know?'" Ibn al-Sammak (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "How many who remind others of Allah are forgetful of Allah! How many who make others fear Allah are bold against Allah! How many who bring others near to Allah are far from Allah! How many who call to Allah flee from Allah! And how many who recite the Book of Allah are detached from the verses of Allah!" And Ibrahim ibn Adham (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "We have made our speech grammatically exact and made no mistake in it, yet we made mistakes in our deeds and did not make them exact."
Al-Awza'i said, "When grammatical inflection (i'rab) comes, humility in prayer (khushu') departs."
Makhul reported from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm that he said, "Ten told me

of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him). They said, "We were studying knowledge in the mosque of Quba' when the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) came out to us and said, 'Learn whatever you wish to learn, for Allah will not reward you until you act.'" (١) Jesus (peace be upon him) said, "The likeness of one who learns knowledge and does not act on it is that of a woman who committed adultery in secret and became pregnant; her pregnancy showed, and she was disgraced. So too, whoever does not act on his knowledge, Allah Most High will disgrace him on the Day of Resurrection before all the witnesses."
Mu'adh (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "Beware the slip of the scholar, because his standing among people is great, so they follow him in his slip."

'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "When the scholar slips, a whole world of people slips with his slip." And 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "Three things bring down the age; one of them is the slip of a scholar."

Ibn Mas'ud said, "A time will come upon the people when the sweetness of hearts turns salty, so on that day neither the scholar nor the student will benefit from knowledge. The hearts of their scholars will be like salt marshes of saline soil, upon which rain from the sky falls and no sweetness is found in them. That is when the hearts of the scholars incline to love of this world and to preferring it over the Hereafter. At that time Allah Most High takes from them the springs of wisdom and extinguishes the lamps of guidance from their hearts. Their scholar will tell you, when you meet him, that he fears Allah with his tongue, while wickedness is apparent in his deeds. How fertile the tongues will be that day, and how barren the hearts! By Allah, besides Whom there is no god, that is only because the teachers taught for other than Allah Most High and the learners learned for other than Allah Most High."
It is written in the Torah and the Gospel: "Do not seek knowledge of what you do not know until you act upon what you know."

Hudhayfa (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "You are in a time in which whoever abandons a tenth of what he knows is destroyed. A time will come in which whoever acts on a tenth of what he knows is saved, and that is because of the great number of the idle."

Know that the likeness of the scholar is that of the judge. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "Judges are three: a judge who judged with the truth while knowing it, and he is in Paradise; a judge who judged unjustly, whether he knew or did not know, and he is in the Fire; and a judge who judged by other than what Allah commanded, and he is in the Fire." (٢) Ka'b (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "At the end of time there will be scholars who make people renounce this world while they do not renounce it, who make people fear while they do not fear, who forbid frequenting the rulers yet come to them, and who prefer this world to the Hereafter. They eat by means of their tongues, drawing the rich near and not the poor. They are jealous over knowledge as women are jealous over men; one of them becomes angry with his companion if he sits with someone else. Those are the tyrants, the enemies of the Most Merciful."

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "Satan may put you off with knowledge." It was said, "Messenger of Allah, how is that?" He (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "He says: Seek knowledge and do not act until you know. So he remains one who speaks of knowledge and puts off action until he dies, and he has not acted." (٣) Sari al-Saqati said, "A man who had been eager to seek outward knowledge withdrew for worship. I asked him, and he said, 'I saw in a dream someone saying to me: How long will you waste knowledge? May Allah waste you! I said: I do memorize it. He said: Preserving knowledge is acting on it. So I left seeking and turned to action.'"

Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "Knowledge is not through abundance of narration; knowledge is only fear of Allah (khashya)." Al-Hasan said, "Learn whatever you wish to learn, for by Allah, Allah will not reward you until you act. The foolish have narration as their concern, while the scholars have observance as their concern." Malik (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "Seeking knowledge is indeed good, and spreading it is indeed good when the intention in it is sound. But look at what is required of you from the time you rise in the morning until the time you reach evening, and prefer nothing over it."

Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "The Qur'an was revealed to be acted upon, yet you have made studying it a work. A people will come who set it straight like a spear shaft; they are not the best of you. The scholar who does not act is like the sick man who describes the medicine, and like the hungry man who describes the delights of foods and does not find them."
